P04.title: P04 reel · same height, three answers (Facebook only; IG published 25.10 manually)

fb.caption:
Three riders. All 178 cm. Three different answers on the same Canyon Grail.

Rider A: inseam 84 cm, typical flexibility, balanced position → M fits best (96%).
Rider B: inseam 88 cm, very flexible, sporty → S (79%). M drops to 62%.
Rider C: inseam 80 cm, stiff back, comfort → M 93%, L 92%.

Your inseam sets the saddle height. Your flexibility and the position you want decide how low and how far the bars should be. That's what picks the size, not your height.

P05.title: Geometry 101 part 2 · frame vs handlebar numbers

ig.caption:
Geometry charts list frame stack and reach. But you don't hold the frame. You hold the handlebar.

Between the two sit the spacers (they lift the bars) and the stem (it pushes them forward).

Canyon Grail Gen 2 (M) vs Specialized Crux (56), on the chart: the Grail frame is 13 mm taller and 14 mm longer.

As sold, the Grail has a 70 mm stem and the Crux a 100 mm stem. So at the handlebar the Crux puts your hands 16 mm further forward (486 vs 470 mm).

16 mm further = a lower, more stretched position. Great if you're flexible, harder on a stiff back and neck. Neither bike is better. It's about which one fits you.

Geomo scores every bike as it's sold, with the factory stem and typical spacers, and shows frame and handlebar numbers side by side. If a different stem would fit you better, it tells you.

ig.caption:
Fit is how you sit. Geometry also decides how a bike rides. Five numbers worth knowing:

Head angle (HTA): slacker = calmer, steeper = quicker steering. Gravel bikes in size M: 69.5° to 72°.

Trail: more = holds a line, less = turns in fast. Published values: 59 to 86 mm.

Wheelbase: longer = steadier, shorter = nimbler. 1011 to 1082 mm.

Chainstay: short = lively, long = planted, with room for big tyres. 420 to 450 mm.

BB drop: more = you sit lower and steadier, but with less room for rocks and a pedal that can touch down mid-corner. Less = more clearance, a bit less steady. 65 to 83 mm.

Neither end is better. It depends on how and where you ride.

In Geomo, fit % comes first. The Target score then adds handling, so you find a bike that fits and rides the way you want. Free, no account. Link in bio.
